profiles.name: Tony Anderson
profiles.description: Tony Anderson was a U.S. Army private who refused deployment to Iraq in July 2008 because of his opposition to taking human life. At a Fort Carson court-martial in November 2008, he received a fourteen-month confinement sentence and a dishonorable discharge for desertion with intent to avoid hazardous duty and disobeying a lawful order. He described difficulties pursuing conscientious-objector status. The sentence is documented; the exact release date and total time served have not been established here.
profiles.finding: Denver ABC release report corroborates resister; Marine master gunnery sergeant, runner and Florida booking namesakes rejected. Possible duplicate Anthony Michael Anderson requires separate audit.

profiles.name: Daniel Sandate
profiles.description: Daniel Sandate was a U.S. Army veteran of Iraq who left the military and lived in Canada before being deported to the United States in 2008. Contemporary reporting describes serious mental-health problems as central to his departure, rather than an initial claim of conscientious objection. He received an eight-month confinement sentence and a bad-conduct discharge, and was released from the Fort Sill brig on January 20, 2009. His case belongs to the broader history of Iraq-era military resistance and treatment of returning veterans; the sentence is not the same as his verified time served.
profiles.finding: War Resisters Support Campaign/Canada coverage corroborates case; surname aggregator and Mexico LinkedIn entries not independently linked. No verified portrait.

profiles.name: Anthony Michael Anderson
profiles.description: Anthony Michael Anderson was a U.S. Army soldier who pled guilty to desertion and disobeying an order in November 2008 and was sentenced to 14 months in military confinement at Fort Sill.
profiles.finding: Nuclear Resister152 lists full name; possible duplicate Tony Anderson flagged, no merge performed. No verified portrait.

profiles.name: Matthew DePalma
profiles.description:
Anarchist convicted of illegally possessing Molotov cocktails allegedly intended to be used at the 2008 Republican National Convention in St. Paul. Arrested on August 30, 2008 by FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force agents at a Minneapolis residence after being surveilled by a paid informant who met him at a CrimethInc Convergence near Waldo, Wisconsin. Pleaded guilty October 21, 2008 to one count of possession of a destructive device.

Matthew Bradley DePalma, age 24, an anarchist, was charged with possession of an unregistered destructive device for preparing Molotov cocktails to be used at the 2008 Republican National Convention in Minneapolis. He unwittingly told his plan to an FBI informant. Pleaded guilty; 42 months federal prison plus 3 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: Denver ABC labels Matt Depalma image from MLive. Download https://i0.wp.com/blog.mlive.com/newsnow_impact/2008/09/depalma.jpg returned404. MPR lead retains photo credit Caroline Yang but subject not verified.

profiles.name: Akram Musa Abdallah
profiles.description: Akram Musa Abdallah, also known as Abu Saiaf, was born in Jericho, Jordan, on July 5, 1954 and later became a naturalized U.S. citizen living in Mesa, Arizona. He helped organize and coordinate Holy Land Foundation fundraising events in the Phoenix area between 1994 and 1997. Federal agents charged him with falsely denying that activity during January 2007 interviews. Abdallah pleaded guilty on May 6, 2009 to making false statements. On March 4, 2010, he was sentenced to 18 months in federal prison and three years of supervised release. He surrendered on June 1, 2010 and was released on September 16, 2011.
profiles.finding: Judgment and indictment corroborate full name; social aggregator namesakes not linked. No portrait verified.

profiles.name: Andrew Smulian
profiles.description: Andrew Smulian, age 67, a South African pilot, was the cooperating co-conspirator who helped DEA agents charge Russian arms dealer Viktor Bout. Pleaded guilty in 2008; 60 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: VOA and Irish Times corroborate Bout witness; prominent images identify Viktor Bout, not Smulian. No portrait verified.

profiles.name: Robin Long
profiles.description: Specialist Robin Long was a U.S. Army soldier who refused deployment to Iraq in 2005 and went absent without leave. He fled to Canada and applied for refugee status, but was denied; in July 2008 he became the first U.S. Iraq War deserter to be deported from Canada to the United States. He was court-martialed at Fort Carson, Colorado, on August 22, 2008, convicted of desertion, and sentenced to 15 months in military confinement plus a dishonorable discharge. He served his sentence at the Naval Consolidated Brig at Miramar, California.
profiles.finding: Verified single-person Robin Long portrait credited to resisters.ca in contemporary Indybay report; deployed unchanged 200x214 original. See batch59.json for credit and rights, deployment and verification files.

profiles.name: Aaron Ellringer
profiles.description: Aaron Ellringer pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor for his limited role in the July 20, 2000 damage to U.S. Forest Service research property near Rhinelander, Wisconsin. Arrested in July 2008, he was sentenced on December 30, 2008 to four credited days in jail.
profiles.finding: Local farmer/cooperative and Kubb portraits are possible leads but not independently linked to ELF defendant; no image added.

profiles.name: Ryan Jackson
profiles.description: Ryan Jackson was a US Army private who sought release from military service on conscientious grounds before deployment to Iraq. He joined antiwar organizing and wrote publicly from the Charleston Naval Brig.
profiles.finding: Courage to Resist image downloaded and visually inspected: campaign graphic with text over scene and full-body figure, not clean portrait. Larger clean source pending.

profiles.name: Jorge De Los Reyes Bautista Martinez
profiles.description:
Jorge Bautista Martinez was caught in an Immigration and Customs Enforcement sting along with nine other co-defendants. Bautista arranged for an undercover informant posing as a FARC member to travel safely through Bogota’s airport. He acted as an intermediary for a smuggling scheme, introduced an informant to his airport immigration contact, and offered to obtain boarding passes for him and secure a Colombian passport and visa. He also ushered the informant through all immigration controls.

Case characteristics: FBI sting operation, FBI confidential informant. Organization referenced in charging documents: FARC.

Case data and description from The Intercept's Trial and Terror project (Trevor Aaronson and Margot Williams), licensed CC BY-NC. Source: https://github.com/theintercept/trial-and-terror-data
profiles.finding: DOJ indictment and UPI/Panama America coverage corroborate case; no verified portrait located.

profiles.name: Frank Ambrose
profiles.description:
Frank Ambrose was an Earth Liberation Front activist and the then-husband of fellow ELF organizer Marius Mason. He participated in numerous Indiana and Michigan ELF actions between 1999 and 2003, including tree-spikings and arsons of homes under construction. After federal investigators tied him to the actions in 2007, he agreed to cooperate with prosecutors and over the following year recorded approximately 178 conversations with Marius Mason and other activists for the FBI. His testimony was the principal basis for the 22-year sentence Mason received in February 2009 — at the time the longest sentence ever imposed on a U.S. eco-defendant.

Ambrose divorced Mason on the day of Mason's arrest. He pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit arson and was sentenced in October 2008 by U.S. District Judge Paul Maloney to 9 years in federal prison; that sentence was later reduced by the same judge to less than six years in light of his cooperation. He served his sentence at federal facilities and has not been publicly active since release. He is widely regarded within the radical-ecology movement as the most consequential federal informant of the Green Scare era; he is included here because he served meaningful federal prison time.
profiles.finding: Animal Liberation Press Office article is identity-specific photo lead; unrelated obituary/genealogy portraits rejected. Original provenance and image verification pending.

profiles.name: Lynne Purvis
profiles.description: Lynne Purvis is an environmental activist jailed after an Everglades-area power-plant blockade. Following release, she spoke about the protest, her trial and conditions in Palm Beach County custody.
profiles.finding: Rising Tide blockade account and Environmental News Network corroborate activist; high-resolution protest-photo archive requires individual identification.

profiles.name: Arthur Landis
profiles.description:
Arthur Landis — SOA Watch line-crosser at Fort Benning, Georgia. Convicted of trespass on a military installation and sentenced to 6 months in federal custody.

Each November on the anniversary of the assassination of six Jesuits, their housekeeper, and her daughter at the University of Central America in San Salvador in 1989, peace activists gather at the gates of Fort Benning, Georgia, site of the U.S. Army School of the Americas / Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation (WHINSEC), to commemorate the dead and to call for the school's closure. Hundreds have crossed the line onto the base over four decades of vigils; many have served federal sentences ranging from 30 days to a year for trespass.
profiles.finding: NYU Arthur H Landis historical photo collection and older obituary are unrelated to SOA Watch profile; no verified portrait located.

profiles.name: Bernardo Valdes Londono
profiles.description:
Bernardo Valdes Londono was caught in an Immigration and Customs Enforcement sting along with nine other co-defendants. Valades offered to provide a fake U.S. visa from a contact in the Colombian federal government and to use his connections at the state comptroller’s office and a district attorney’s office to register an undercover informant, posing as a FARC agent, at the International Red Cross. He presented the informant with a fake Spanish passport, introduced him to someone who could transport bulk quantities of drugs, and provided fake Panamanian immigration stamps.

Case characteristics: FBI sting operation, FBI confidential informant. Organization referenced in charging documents: FARC.

Case data and description from The Intercept's Trial and Terror project (Trevor Aaronson and Margot Williams), licensed CC BY-NC. Source: https://github.com/theintercept/trial-and-terror-data
profiles.finding: DOJ plea release and Colombian judicial records corroborate defendant; no verified portrait located.

profiles.name: James Burmeister
profiles.description: James Burmeister was a U.S. Army Iraq veteran who went to Canada in 2007 rather than redeploy and publicly criticized military tactics he had witnessed. After returning voluntarily, he was court-martialed at Fort Knox, Kentucky, in July 2008 and received a confinement sentence. Contemporary accounts differ on the sentence's length. A report published October 30, 2008 confirmed that he had been released and was home with his family. His exact custody duration and any later discharge upgrade remain unverified.
profiles.finding: Courage to Resist original image downloaded and inspected: 250x191 helmeted soldier with sunglasses, usable lead but clearer obituary or guitar portrait preferred. Mother's rally photo explicitly excluded.

profiles.name: Thirunavukkarasu Varatharasa
profiles.description:
Caught in an Immigration and Customs Enforcement sting along with Haniffa Osman, Reinhard Rusli, Helmi Soedirdja, Erick Wotulo, and Haji Subandi, Thirunavukkarasu Varatharasa intended to buy weapons on behalf of the Tamil Tigers, contacting an undercover FBI business located in Maryland about the sale of weapons. He agreed to send money to an undercover FBI bank account as payment.

Case characteristics: FBI sting operation, FBI confidential informant. Organization referenced in charging documents: Tamil Tigers.

Case data and description from The Intercept's Trial and Terror project (Trevor Aaronson and Margot Williams), licensed CC BY-NC. Source: https://github.com/theintercept/trial-and-terror-data
profiles.finding: Case-related government report corroborates name; Sri Lankan gazette and university partial-name matches rejected. No portrait verified.

profiles.name: Joshua Simpson
profiles.description: Joshua Simpson is an Iraq War combat veteran and former Fort Lewis Army interrogator who became an anti-war organizer and Evergreen State College student. He participated in the November 2007 Port of Olympia protests against the movement of Stryker vehicles and spoke publicly about his experience in Mosul. Contemporaneous coverage places him at the protests, but the available arrest lists and later federal litigation do not establish that he was one of the people arrested, booked or confined.
profiles.finding: Evergreen historian photo page explicitly places Josh Simpson at left in group. Needs clean crop and rights assessment; database biography itself says custody not established, flagged without alteration.

profiles.name: Shyam Prasad Khanna
profiles.description: Shyam Prasad Khanna was a Port Militarization Resistance activist in Olympia, Washington. On November 8, 2007, he ran into the street to block a Stryker vehicle carrying military equipment from the Port of Olympia; police chased and arrested him after the driver swerved. He was later convicted in a case arising from the port protests and served 30 days on work release. The available accounts state the exact sentence length but do not supply the start and end dates of the work-release term.
profiles.finding: Exact-name Olympia search produced no verified individual portrait; federal Port Militarization litigation is contextual lead.
